input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 binds us (the Company) not to participate in any project similar to the Site with respect to Deerskin Products "or products substantially similar" — an open-ended scope extending to "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" rather than a named competing product — and additionally hands HDI an exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand, which is a field-of-use restriction on using and licensing our own brand. It therefore fails the fallback on multiple material terms: scope is not a single named product, there is no 12-month cap (the term auto-renews annually under Section 4.1, so the restriction can run indefinitely), and there are no carve-outs for our internal development or acquisitions. Section 6.2 preserves only a narrow closeout-merchandise carve-out and does not cure this. We therefore target the preferred position and convert Section 6.1 into an express permission, leaving Section 6.3 (which restricts HDI and benefits us) untouched. Separately noted, not flagged: the Section 9(b) proviso requiring termination of the Globix hosting agreement is a sourcing/exclusivity condition rather than a restriction on the businesses or products we may operate or build.

proposal.summary: Remove the non-compete/field-of-use restriction on the Company in Section 6.1, including HDI's exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a restriction on the projects or products we may pursue, or an HDI exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand, so we have converted Section 6.1 into an express permission; our position is no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on the Company. If HDI needs protection, we could discuss a restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
